highlight.title: Next.js Now Includes AGENTS.md by Default - AI-First Development
highlight.summary: <cite index="1-15">The default setup enables TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, App Router, and Turbopack, with import alias @/*, and includes AGENTS.md (with a CLAUDE.md that references it) to guide coding agents to write up-to-date Next.js code.</cite> This represents a fundamental shift toward AI-first development workflows in modern web applications.

resources.title: React 19 Server Components: Production Patterns for High-Performance Apps
resources.why_now: <cite index="16-2">React 19 Server Components represent a fundamental shift in web architecture from "client-side data fetching" to a "server-first" model with 74% reduction in JS bundle size and 45% improvement in time to interactive.</cite>

resources.title: Better Auth vs NextAuth: The Authentication Battle of 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="35-8,35-9">NextAuth started falling apart when building B2B SaaS that needed email OTP, two-factor authentication, passkeys, organization support, and multi-session management - Better Auth v1.5.3 solved all these issues.</cite>

resources.title: The JavaScript Stack in 2026: What Every Developer Needs to Know
resources.why_now: <cite index="22-28,22-29">With React Server Components, server actions, and edge functions blurring where code actually runs, understanding the client-server boundary deeply shapes security, performance, and architecture simultaneously.</cite>

resources.title: TypeScript Developer Guide 2026: Why Every Full Stack Developer Needs It
resources.why_now: <cite index="25-4,25-6">In 2026, writing production JavaScript without TypeScript feels like driving without a seatbelt - TypeScript has evolved from a nice-to-have tool into the de facto standard for full stack development.</cite>

claude_take: The ecosystem has reached an inflection point where React 19 Server Components aren't experimental anymore - they're production-ready with proven 40-70% performance gains. The most interesting development is Next.js shipping with AI guidance files by default, signaling that LLM-assisted development is becoming the expected workflow, not an edge case.
